steps: Start with the pyramid: 4 sloping faces and 1 base = 5.
Each triangular tunnel adds its own inner walls.
Where the two tunnels cross inside, their walls are cut into extra pieces.
Counting every separate flat face gives 14.
qs.trap: Adding just 3 + 3 for the tunnels. Where tunnels cross, walls split into more faces.

steps: Work row by row: A has four first steps.
In each row, count the parallel links between the two nodes, then the routes onward to B.
Paths in a row = parallel links × onward routes.
Add all four rows: 32.
qs.trap: Counting the parallel arcs as one link. Each arc is a separate route.

steps: Each word is split into two halves: top or left parts in one word, the rest in the other.
Overlay the two coded words to rebuild the full letters.
Check with ART and TEXT that the rule works.
The third line rebuilds to the digits 836975.
qs.trap: Reading the code symbols as ordinary letters. They only make sense when overlaid.

steps: Look at the edges of each spine: rivers, paths and coastlines must continue across.
Find the left-most spine (map edge on the left) and the right-most.
Join spines whose features line up exactly.
qs.trap: Matching only one feature. Check the river, path and coastline all line up.

steps: y = 5, so stop. x = 24.

qs.note: Watch the whole loop and count only frames that show all six features. Morphing in-between frames are not faces. On paper only one frame is shown, so practise this type with animations.

steps: PQS and QRS are equilateral triangles sharing side QS. PR is two of their heights, so each height is 10.5.
The circle through P, Q and S has radius equal to two-thirds of the height: 7.
Black = circle − white triangle PQS + black triangle QRS.
The two triangles are equal, so black = circle = 22/7 × 49 = 154.

steps: Take the square side as 2: the circle has radius 1, the semicircle radius 1.
The diagonal is a line of symmetry for the circle.
Match each blue piece with an equal white piece across the diagonal or the semicircle.
The blue pieces add up to one quarter of the square.
qs.trap: Starting long calculations. Symmetry questions usually have a neat fraction.

steps: Readers of at least one: 200 − 50 = 150.
Only X = 30, only Y = 50.
Exactly one = 30 + 50 = 80.

qs.trap: Answering 150. That includes the 70 who read both.

steps: Look at each partial letter and imagine what is missing: a curve, a bar or a diagonal.
Match each part in row 2 by shape and width.
Write the part numbers in the order of the letters.
The order is 5, 7, 2, 4, 3, 6, 1.
qs.trap: Matching by height only. Widths and curve directions also matter.

steps: The original square has perimeter 40.
The notch removes some outer edge but adds the same length on its inner side.
It also adds two sides of the small square, 5 each.
Perimeter = 40 + 10 = 50.
qs.trap: Subtracting the notch. Cutting into a shape usually increases the perimeter.

steps: So Y + 17 = 3Y − 9, giving Y = 13 and X = 30.
Sum = 43.

qs.trap: Writing 3Y − 3 instead of 3 (Y − 3). Brackets matter.

steps: Red is under 3 marbles in P, and R already holds 4 marbles that must leave.
Q has room for only 3 more; P and R share the rest of the space.
Plan moves so marbles from R and P use the free spaces without blocking red.
We checked every sequence by computer search: the minimum is 10 moves.

steps: Mark every right angle in the figure: rectangle corners and perpendicular crossings.
From each right angle, look for a third line closing a triangle.
Count small and large triangles at each right angle.
The total is 18.
qs.trap: Counting triangles that only look square-cornered. Check the lines really are perpendicular.

steps: Each stick balances when weight × distance is equal on both sides of its string.
Start at the bottom stick: blue balances black.
Move up one stick at a time, using the total weight hanging below each string.
Working up to the top stick gives red = 60 g.
qs.trap: Assuming every string hangs from the middle. Measure each arm from the figure.

steps: Speed × diameter is the same across a belt or a mesh.
M › N: 100 × 3 = N × 1, so N = 300. N meshes with P: P = 150.
Q is on P's axle: 150. Q › R by belt: R = 150 × 1 ÷ 3 = 50.
R meshes with S: S = 50 × 3 ÷ 2 = 75 rpm.

steps: This solid is a rhombicosidodecahedron.
Each pentagon is surrounded by squares; each square sits between a pentagon and a triangle.
It has 12 pentagons, 30 squares and 20 triangles.
Check with Euler: V 60, E 120, F 62: 60 − 120 + 62 = 2.

font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="start">62</text><line x1="2" y1="99" x2="232" y2="99" stroke="#E8DFC8" stroke-width="0.6" stroke-linecap="round" /></svg>
qs.trap: Counting only the visible squares. Use symmetry: one pentagon's 5 squares × 12 ÷ 2 = 30.

steps: Equal perimeters: if the hexagon side is a, the triangle side is 2a.
Triangle inradius = 2a ÷ (2 root 3) = a ÷ root 3.
Hexagon inradius = a × root 3 ÷ 2.
Ratio = 3/2, so the blue circle = 10 × 1.5 = 15 cm.
qs.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 236 136" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="4" y="4" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="19" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Same perimeter: triangle side = 2 × hexagon side</text><rect x="4" y="30" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="45" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Triangle inradius = side ÷ (2 root 3) = a ÷ root 3</text><rect x="4" y="56" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="71" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Hexagon inradius = a × root 3 ÷ 2</text><rect x="4" y="82" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="97" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Ratio = (root 3 ÷ 2) ÷ (1 ÷ root 3) = 3/2</text><rect x="4" y="108" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#FFE3CF" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="123" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="700" fill="#FF6B0A" text-anchor="start">Blue = 10 × 1.5 = 15 cm</text></svg>
qs.trap: Assuming equal sides. Equal perimeters mean the triangle's side is twice the hexagon's.

steps: Find the smallest repeating unit of the pattern.
A full circle, repeated on a grid with overlaps, recreates the pattern (A).
The four-pointed concave star is the gap shape between circles; repeated, it also traces all the arcs (D).
B and C leave out arcs or add lines.
qs.trap: Thinking only one block can work. Different units can tile the same pattern.

steps: Note each hole's shape and position around the socket.
Turn each plug until one pin matches its hole.
Then check that every other pin lines up with its hole.
A and D fit; B and C have a pin in the wrong place.
qs.trap: Checking pin shapes but not their order around the circle.

steps: Rewrite: y = log 25 ÷ log x.
Check points: x = 5 gives y = 2; x = 25 gives y = 1.
Near x = 1 the curve shoots up; for x between 0 and 1, y is negative.
C passes through (5, 2) and (25, 1); D also shows the negative branch.
qs.trap: Treating it like xy = 25, a different curve. Test exact points.

steps: Count the lines meeting at each point (its degree).
A figure can be drawn in one stroke if every point has an even degree, or exactly two are odd.
Check each figure's junctions.
A, B and D pass; C has more than two odd points.
qs.trap: Trying to draw by trial. The even-degree rule answers instantly.

steps: A solid passes through a hole if one of its outlines (front, side or top) fits.
Find the outline of the solid from each direction.
Match each cut-out to one of those outlines.
A, C and D each match one outline.
qs.trap: Checking only one direction. Any orientation is allowed.

steps: A stool is stable if the person's weight on the top step falls inside the base area of its feet.
Look at where the top step sits compared with the feet.
If the top step overhangs beyond the feet, it tips.
A and D keep the top step over the base.
qs.trap: Judging by how many legs it has. Position of the weight matters more.

steps: A tile fits with copies of itself when every bump matches a dent on the opposite side.
Check top against bottom and left against right.
Shifted rows, as in Y, are allowed.
A and D tile; B and C leave gaps.
qs.trap: Choosing a nice-looking animal shape without checking the edges.

steps: Note the shape: count cubes and see how they join.
Note the face markings (squares and ovals) and their positions.
Turn each option until the shape matches, then check the markings.
B, C and D match.
qs.trap: Matching shape but ignoring markings.

steps: A knot forms only if the rope truly passes through itself, not just over.
Follow the rope from one end and note over and under crossings.
If you can slide crossings apart without passing an end through, it unravels.
B and D form knots; A and C pull straight.
qs.trap: Counting crossings. Many crossings can still unravel.

steps: Count P's squares; each piece must be one quarter of that.
Rule out pieces with the wrong number of squares.
Try fitting four copies of the remaining pieces into P.
A and B work.
qs.trap: Skipping the area check, which removes wrong options at once.

steps: The water surface always stays level, whatever the tilt.
The block stays fixed to the side it rests on.
The amount of water does not change, so check the water area looks the same.
A and C show this correctly.
qs.trap: Tilting the water surface with the box.

steps: Each piece is two coloured cubes stuck together.
In each option, find each colour pair: they must be next to each other.
If two cubes from the same piece are apart, the option is impossible.
B and D are impossible.
qs.trap: Forgetting that the question asks which are NOT possible.

steps: Note the tile's layout: the corner colours and the small purple squares.
Each pattern is the tile repeated and rotated.
Divide each pattern into tile-sized squares and check each one.
A and B can be made.
qs.trap: Accepting a pattern with one tile that is mirrored.

steps: Note each piece's angles and lengths.
Find the distinctive pieces in each shape first: the notched one and the long one.
Check that the remaining pieces fill the rest.
A, C and D work.
qs.trap: Accepting a shape that needs a fifth piece.

steps: Count board squares and the squares in the six pieces.
The extra pieces must make up the difference.
Then check that they fit the remaining space.
A and D complete the board.
qs.trap: Skipping the area count.

steps: A rocker needs one smooth curve touching the floor.
Bumps or flat steps stop smooth rocking.
A stub or extra foot also stops it.
A and D rock.
qs.trap: Choosing any curved base. Only one smooth arc rocks.

steps: Find P's distinctive marks: the rounded corners in some cells.
Rotate P by 90°, 180° and 270° and see where those marks go.
A mirrored copy is not a rotation.
A and B are rotations.
qs.trap: Accepting a mirror image as a rotation.

steps: The line must flow smoothly across each fold.
Follow the line from face to face in the net.
Check each cube: does the line meet each edge in the same place?
A and C match.
qs.trap: Checking only one face.

steps: From the back, left and right swap.
Each clip shows its other loop, so the shapes change.
The punched holes move to the other side.
Option A shows all of this.
qs.trap: Just flipping the image. The clips themselves look different from behind.

steps: Track one symbol through the sequence: the yin-yang, for example.
Find how the whole tile turns each step.
Apply the turn once more.
Option B matches.
qs.trap: Tracking symbols separately when the whole tile rotates.

steps: Two flips at right angles = a 180° turn.
So the circles move from the top to the bottom, in the same order outwards.
A 180° turn keeps the direction of spinning.
Option D shows this.
qs.trap: Reversing the spin. Two flips cancel each other's mirror effect.

steps: Read each box carefully: some are worded negatively.
"Do not notify me on Promotions": you want promotions, so skip.
"Do not allow access to my Contacts": you want to block, so check.
Skip, skip, check, check, check, check: option D.

qs.trap: Checking every box that mentions what you want. Negative wording flips the action.

steps: The spider is above, so we look down at Sabina.
Her face and head look big; her legs look short and far away.
She is looking up at the spider, so we see her face, with the body small and far below.
Option D shows this best.
qs.trap: Choosing a top view of the back of her head. She is looking up at the spider.

steps: A mirror swaps left and right but keeps top and bottom.
Choose two small details, like the dashes on each side, and swap them.
Check each option for both details.
Option C matches.
qs.trap: Choosing a rotated copy. Mirror images cannot be made by turning.

steps: The sphere touches the ground at one point; the shadow starts there.
Light at an angle stretches the shadow into an ellipse away from the light.
The ellipse is longer than the sphere is wide, and part of it lies under the sphere itself.
Option A shows this.
qs.trap: Drawing a circle. Slanted light makes an ellipse.

steps: A stencil cuts out the letters; the inner parts (like the centre of o, e, d, a, p, g) would fall out.
Working stencils keep small bridges to hold those centres.
Check each design for bridges in every closed letter.
Design C lacks bridges, so it fails.
qs.trap: Choosing the ugliest design. The test is whether the centres stay attached.

steps: With the Sun overhead, shadows fall straight down, right under each person.
Tops of heads and shoulders are bright; faces are shaded from above.
Light patches come through gaps in the leaves.
Option A shows this.
qs.trap: Choosing long shadows. Overhead sun gives very short shadows.

steps: Look at how each symbol is built: parts mirrored or repeated.
Find the rule three symbols share.
Check which symbol breaks it.
D is the odd one.
qs.trap: Judging by size or weight instead of construction.

steps: Opposite faces never touch in a net; they are separated by one face in a row.
Find each pair in each net and check they are opposite.
Then check the diagonal lines and dots meet correctly at a corner.
Only C works.
qs.trap: Checking opposite pairs but not the direction of the diagonals.

steps: Track one fragment through the grids.
Find the rule: how positions and shades change.
Apply it once more.
Option C fits.
qs.trap: Tracking all fragments at once.

steps: Use real sizes: Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra are larger than Gujarat and West Bengal.
Compare the drawn sizes with the real ones.
West Bengal (D) is far smaller than the others in reality, yet it is drawn almost as large.
D is the scaled map.
qs.trap: Thinking all maps should look the same size. They should match real proportions.

steps: Three photos are the same arrangement, only turned.
Check the order of objects around the plate in each photo.
One photo has a different order: that is Shefali's.
Option A has a different order.
qs.trap: Looking at angles instead of the order of objects around the plate.

steps: Count branches and note their heights and directions.
Note which branches are open tubes and which are solid.
Turn each option to match.
Option A matches.
qs.trap: Ignoring which branches are hollow.

steps: Every line entering the gap must continue and close a triangle.
Follow each line to the gap's edge and note its direction.
Check which option continues every line correctly.
Option A does.
qs.trap: Choosing a piece that looks similar but leaves some lines unfinished.

steps: Each reflection mirrors the arrows.
An even number of reflections cancels the mirroring, leaving a rotation.
Six reflections give a rotated copy with arrows turning the same way as the start.
Option B shows this.

qs.trap: Mirroring the final figure. Six is even: the result is not mirrored.

steps: Look at the rows and columns of large and small squares around the gap.
The missing piece must continue each row and column.
Check the edges of each option.
Option A fits.
qs.trap: Matching only one edge.

steps: A one-sheet zine folds so the bottom row becomes the cover and back.
The cover is W; the pages then go along the top row backwards: S, R, Q, P.
The bottom row then finishes the booklet: T, U, V.
Order: W, S, R, Q, P, T, U, V.
qs.trap: Reading the panels in printed order. Folding reverses the top row.

steps: Pick distinctive slices: the cat, the laptop and the window.
Check each option for those slices, unchanged.
Then check that no slice is mirrored or edited.
B is correct.
qs.trap: Accepting a slice with a small change, such as a missing object.

steps: Halving an ink makes it lighter.
Cyan at 50% is a light blue; black at 50% is a mid grey.
Together they make a greyish blue.
Option D is the grey-blue.
qs.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 290 112" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="20" cy="26" r="14" fill="#F48FB1" stroke="none" stroke-width="1.4"/><text x="42" y="30" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="middle">+</text><circle cx="64" cy="26" r="14" fill="#FFF59D" stroke="none" stroke-width="1.4"/><text x="86" y="30" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="middle">=</text><circle cx="108" cy="26" r="16" fill="#F4A07F" stroke="none" stroke-width="1.4"/><text x="132" y="30" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">magenta 50 + yellow 50 = coral</text><circle cx="20" cy="78" r="14" fill="#81D4FA" stroke="none" stroke-width="1.4"/><text x="42" y="82" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="middle">+</text><circle cx="64" cy="78" r="14" fill="#9E9E9E" stroke="none" stroke-width="1.4"/><text x="86" y="82" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#5A6278" text-anchor="middle">=</text><circle cx="108" cy="78" r="16" fill="#4F7F95" stroke="none" stroke-width="1.4"/><text x="132" y="82" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">cyan 50 + black 50 = grey-blue</text></svg>
qs.trap: Choosing a green. Green needs yellow, which is not used here.

steps: INDIAN uses high-contrast letters: very thick and very thin strokes with fine serifs.
Compare each S for the same contrast and serif style.
Check the S weight matches the other letters.
A matches.
qs.trap: Choosing a lighter serif S. Contrast is the key feature here.

steps: A closed fan stacks all its pleats together, folded like an accordion.
It is dipped at a slant, so the dye line crosses each pleat at an angle.
When opened, neighbouring pleats face opposite ways, so the slanted lines form zigzags.
Option A shows zigzag band edges in the right order: red outside, orange inside.
qs.trap: Expecting smooth arcs. The pleats and the slanted dip create zigzags.

steps: Road art is designed to look right from one viewpoint, seen at a low angle.
Seen at a low angle, things far away look squashed, so the plan must undo that.
Compare each plan's proportions with the photo.
The official answer is C.
qs.trap: Choosing the plan that looks exactly like the photo.

steps: Each side: corner + 2 middles + corner = 10. Corners count for two sides.
Total cards = 4 × 10 − sum of corners.
Now: corners 1, 4, 1, 4 sum to 10, so 30 cards.
Most possible: corners all 1, 36 cards. 36 − 30 = 6.

qs.trap: Forgetting corners are shared by two sides.

steps: From behind, left and right swap.
The kicking leg and ball appear on the opposite side.
We see her back and hair, not her face, and the ball looks the right size for its distance.
Option C shows this.
qs.trap: Keeping the ball on the same side.

steps: Compare outline details: claws, horns, whiskers and the tail.
Check gaps inside the outline, which show as holes.
Find the option where every detail matches.
A matches.
qs.trap: Checking only the big shape.

steps: Follow each path from its fly, using your finger.
Count each glass the path passes over.
Do not switch paths where lines cross.
Fly B crosses the most.
qs.trap: Switching to another path at a crossing.

steps: Ha Lan = Netherlands, Ao = Austria, Ba Lan = Poland: all three are right.
In A, Phan Lan is Finland, not Poland.
In C, Ha Lan is the Netherlands, not Finland.
In D, Na Uy is Norway and Thuy Dien is Sweden.

steps: A smooth ride needs the wheel's centre to stay at the same height.
Each wheel shape is paired with a road shaped to keep its centre level, more or less.
Look for the pairing where the centre rises and falls most: the teardrop on big arches.
D gives the bumpiest ride.
qs.trap: Choosing the strangest wheel. The match with the road decides.

steps: The pin enters a slot of Q, turns Q a quarter turn, then leaves.
While the pin is out, Q is locked still.
Meshing turns Q the opposite way to P.
So Q turns anticlockwise in steps: intermittently.
qs.trap: Choosing continuous motion. A Geneva drive moves in steps.
